'''Joseph Reshard Crawford II''' (born June 17, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] and was selected with the 58th overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He signed with the Lakers on August 27, 2008,<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3556514 Crawford, Lakers' lone draftee, comes to terms]</ref> but was waived October 22, during the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 pre-season]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/081022lakerswaivecrawfordgiles.html LAKERS WAIVE JOE CRAWFORD AND CJ GILES]</ref>

==High school and recruitment==
Crawford attended [[Renaissance High School (Michigan)|Renaissance High School]] in Detroit, where he led his team to a perfect 27–0 record and a state title.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3420/joe-crawford ESPN.com Player Profile - Joe Crawford]</ref> He was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite news |author1=John Clay |title=Conference play bringing out Crawford's best |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99048474/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=17 January 2007 |pages=D1, D8 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref> Crawford originally committed to play for the [[University of Michigan]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?Sport=2&pr_key=12300 |title=Rivals.com Basketball Recruiting - Joe Crawford |access-date=September 13, 2006 |archive-date=February 21, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080221001353/http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?Sport=2&pr_key=12300 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but reopened his recruitment and chose to attend the [[University of Kentucky]]<ref>{{cite news |author1=Matt May |title=Crawford saga result of larger epidemic |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99048918/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |work=[[The Messenger (Madisonville, Kentucky)|The Messenger]] |date=19 January 2005 |page=D6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref> as part of a freshman class that also featured [[Ramel Bradley]] and All-Americans [[Rajon Rondo]] and [[Randolph Morris]].

==College career==
Crawford became a bigger part of the team's rotation in his sophomore season, averaging 10.2 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sportsline.com/collegebasketball/players/playerpage/524758 |title=CBS Sportsline Player Profile - Joe Crawford |access-date=September 13, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060524024206/http://www.sportsline.com/collegebasketball/players/playerpage/524758 |archive-date=May 24, 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During his junior year, Crawford started 32 of 34 games and averaged 14 points, 4 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game. He was the leading scorer in 8 games and set a new career high in an overtime loss against the [[Georgia Bulldogs]] with 29 points.

Crawford became the 54th Wildcat to score 1,000 points in his career<ref>[https://www.espn.com/espn/columns/story?columnist=forde_pat&id=3146892 Younger Crawford, Indiana get best of Kentucky]</ref> on December 1, 2007, against the [[North Carolina Tarheels]].

On March 20, 2008, Crawford closed his career with a loss to [[Marquette University|Marquette Golden Eagles]] in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]]. Crawford was the game's high scorer, matching a career-best with 35 points before fouling out.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080325014314/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000023 McNeal, Marquette get by Kentucky, nab first tourney win since 2003]</ref>

==Professional career==
Joe Crawford was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the 58th overall pick in the second round of the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He signed with the Lakers on August 27, 2008. Crawford was waived by the [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]] on October 22, 2008. Crawford had played in all three exhibition games during the [[NBA]] pre-season, averaging 8.3 minutes and 2.7 points. Crawford had to make the team in order for his contract to be guaranteed. Crawford then played in the [[NBA Development League]] for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] affiliate [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]]. On March 26, 2009, Crawford was called up from the D-League by the [[New York Knicks]] and signed a 10-day contract.<ref name="Knicks Sign">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/crawford_090327.html |title=Knicks Sign Los Angeles' Joe Crawford |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 27, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329073539/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/crawford_090327.html |archive-date=March 29, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 6, 2009, he signed with the Knicks for the rest of the season. On October 22, 2009, Joe Crawford was waived from the Knicks' roster.<ref name="NBA.com">[http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/crawfordhunterwaived.html Knicks Waive Crawford and Hunter]</ref>

After playing for the Orlando Magic's summer league team in the summer of 2010, Crawford signed a non-guaranteed contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://susanshan.com/2010/08/25/joe-crawfords-nba-dream-alive/ |title=Joe Crawford's NBA Dream is Alive and Well |access-date=August 28, 2010 |archive-date=April 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160404135907/http://susanshan.com/2010/08/25/joe-crawfords-nba-dream-alive/ |url-status=usurped }}</ref> He was released on October 15.
Joe Crawford then joined his former [[University of Kentucky]] teammate [[Randolph Morris]] on the [[Beijing Ducks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.allkyhoops.com/2011/01/joe-crawford-to-join-randolph-morris-in.html |title=Joe Crawford to Join Randolph Morris in China | AllKyHoops.com |access-date=March 11, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324173202/http://www.allkyhoops.com/2011/01/joe-crawford-to-join-randolph-morris-in.html |archive-date=March 24, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He later played with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] of Israel.

On January 18, 2015, he was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4917117 BayHawks Acquire Crawford, Waive Provost]</ref> On October 12, he left Erie to sign in the newly formed AmeriLeague;<ref>{{cite news|title=Joe Crawford Signs With AmeriLeague|url=http://www.amerileague.com/blog/joe-crawford-signs-with-amerileague/|access-date=October 12, 2015|work=AmeriLeague.com|date=October 12, 2015}}</ref> however, the league folded after it was discovered the founder was a con-artist.<ref>{{cite news|title=AmeriLeague Founder Revealed As Con Artist|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/239602/AmeriLeague-Founder-Revealed-As-Con-Artist|access-date=October 22, 2015|work=RealGM.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Crawford's brother, [[Jordan Crawford]], played [[college basketball]] for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]]<ref>{{cite news |author1=Terry Hutchens |title=IU's Crawford wins matchup against his older brother |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99048620/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=9 December 2007 |page=C9 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Terry Hutchens |title=Oh, brother! |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99048840/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=8 December 2007 |pages=D1, D6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{open access}}</ref> and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]]; he also played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]].
